title: The Postcard of the Crescent Cove
premise: Rosalind Blackwood, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter and part-time novelist, has kept her heart in the past tense ever since Theo Marsh left Crescent Cove a decade ago without saying goodbye. When the town's winter festival assigns anonymous pen pals to boost morale, a clerical error pairs Rosalind not with a stranger but with Theo — who has returned to save his family's failing bakery, and who has been secretly writing to her for years under a false name. As their letters deepen and their daytime sparring sharpens, Rosalind discovers the deception and must choose between loyalty to her wounded pride and the truth that Theo's rehearsed apology was always meant for her. The lease clock ticking, he finally speaks the sentence he has carried for ten years, and she answers not with a letter but in person, at the lighthouse where it all began.
about_author: Elodie Okafor is a former coastal archivist who spent three years cataloguing lighthouse logs before turning to fiction full-time. She writes love stories set in small towns where the sea keeps everyone's secrets, and she still answers every letter by hand.

chapters.title: The Tide That Keeps Its Own Time
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She tends the lighthouse, drafts the same first chapter of her novel for the hundredth time, and deflects her grandmother's gentle probing about why she never leaves the cove. Establishes her guarded heart and the town's winter pen-pal tradition. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: A Bakery With Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He returns to Crescent Cove to rescue his late father's bakery before the lease expires in ninety days, dreading the one person he wronged. He sees Rosalind across the harbor and rehearses a sentence he's carried for ten years. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee's Clerical Sin
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The pen-pal assignment goes out; a volunteer's typo pairs Rosalind with 'T. Marsh' under the alias 'Cormorant.' Their first exchange is prickly, anonymous, and unexpectedly alive. Emotional beat: irritation curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Flour on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. By day, Rosalind boycotts his bakery loudly; by night, his letters make her laugh. He recognizes her voice in the prose immediately and realizes she doesn't know who she's writing to. Emotional beat: the intoxication and dread of a secret kept in real time.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Log Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Researching her novel, she finds her grandfather's old logbook and a decade-old entry the night Theo left — evidence his departure wasn't the abandonment she believed. She writes 'Cormorant' the most honest letter she's ever sent. Emotional beat: the first crack in her past tense.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Then Sixty
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The lease deadline halves; his letters to Rosalind become the only place he tells the truth about his father's debts and his own cowardice. A near-miss at the harbor market almost exposes him. Emotional beat: the secret becoming a weight he can no longer lift alone.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Wrong Envelope
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A misdelivered envelope — Theo's handwriting, addressed to 'Cormorant, care of the lighthouse' — lands in her hands. She confronts the bakery at closing time and he confesses everything, including the years of letters. She walks out. Emotional beat: betrayal and recognition colliding.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A winter gale knocks out the cove's power; the lighthouse must be run by hand, and Theo shows up uninvited to help. Through the night, between lamp rotations, the rehearsed sentence finally comes: 'I left because I loved you and thought you'd be better off.' Emotional beat: truth offered, not yet accepted.

chapters.title: Past Tense, Present Company
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the storm's aftermath, she reads every letter he ever sent, then rewrites her novel's ending for the first time. She chooses loyalty to the truth over the safety of her grievance and walks to the bakery as the lease papers sit unsigned. Emotional beat: forgiveness as an act of courage.

chapters.title: The Postcard of the Crescent Cove
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He signs the new lease with Rosalind's name beside his; the festival reveals the pen-pal error to laughter and applause. At the lighthouse, she hands him a postcard — her first chapter, finally finished, dedicated to 'the boy who came back.' Emotional beat: belonging, earned and kept.
